ceo.name: Christopher J. Nassetta
ceo.title: President & Chief Executive Officer
ceo.background: Born 1964, Arlington, VA. UVA + London School of Economics. Started in hospitality at age 16. Co-founded Bailey Capital Corporation (1991, real estate investment/advisory). Joined Host Hotels & Resorts 1995 as EVP, COO by 1997, CEO from 2000-2007. One of longest-serving CEOs in hospitality sector.

track_record.room_growth: More than doubled brand portfolio, global property and room counts since 2007. Expanded to ~140 countries/territories.
track_record.capital_return_2024: $3.0B returned to shareholders via buybacks and dividends
track_record.development_record_2024: Signed record 154,000 rooms for development; opened more rooms than any prior year
track_record.brand_expansion: Portfolio expanded from ~10 brands to 24 brands under his tenure
track_record.asset_light_transformation: Led Hilton's transformation to asset-light model post-Blackstone LBO (2007) and IPO (2013), spinning off Park Hotels & Resorts and Hilton Grand Vacations in 2017

recent_transactions.action: Exercised options for 114,289 shares at $41.41/share; sold 114,289 shares at $316.27-$319.30 weighted average

cfo.name: Kevin J. Jacobs
cfo.title: Chief Financial Officer & President, Global Development (development role through 2025)
cfo.background: Cornell University School of Hotel Administration ('94). Prior: SVP M&A and Treasurer at Fairmont Raffles Hotels International. 7 years at Host Hotels & Resorts (VP Corporate Strategy & IR). Earlier: PwC Hospitality Consulting, Cushman & Wakefield Hospitality Valuation Group.
cfo.career_at_hilton: Joined 2008 as SVP Corporate Strategy → Treasurer (2009) → EVP & Chief of Staff (2012) → CFO (2013). Also served as President, Global Development (2020-2025).
cfo.board_memberships: Board of Directors, Omega Healthcare Investors; Trustee, Cornell University; Dean's Advisory Board, Cornell SHA; Immediate Past Chair, American Hotel & Lodging Association

insider_ownership_pct.note: WallStreetZen reports 39.45% insider ownership but likely includes Blackstone-affiliated holdings. The ~1.78% figure from SEC proxy filings is more conservative and reflects direct/indirect holdings of named officers and directors. Blackstone (Jon Gray is Board Chair) remains a significant institutional holder.
insider_ownership_pct.data_conflict: Multiple sources report widely different insider ownership (1.78% vs 39.45%). The discrepancy likely reflects whether Blackstone's ~20%+ stake is classified as 'insider' given Jon Gray's dual role as Board Chair and Blackstone COO.

compensation_highlights.peer_group: 17 hospitality, travel, and global consumer brands
compensation_highlights.program_structure: Base salary + annual cash bonus + long-term equity (options + restricted stock units)
compensation_highlights.note: Nassetta consistently among highest-paid hotel CEOs globally

governance_notes.board_chair: Jon Gray (President & COO, Blackstone Group; Chairman since 2021)
governance_notes.board_independence: Majority independent directors; Blackstone representation via Gray reflects legacy LBO ownership
governance_notes.blackstone_influence: Blackstone took Hilton private in 2007 ($26B LBO). IPO 2013. Blackstone has gradually reduced stake but Jon Gray remains Board Chair, maintaining strategic influence.
governance_notes.key_risk: Board Chair tied to largest PE firm creates potential governance conflict; mitigated by strong independent committee structure and >90% Say-on-Pay approval
